## Where we are

- **Part 1–2:** writing R, managing projects, structuring data
- **Part 3:** the tidyverse + Git — your *code* is now reproducible
- **Part 4, Hour 1:** a real DESeq2 differential-expression pipeline
- **Part 4, Hour 2 (now):** make the *environment* reproducible too

::: notes
This hour is the capstone. They have working code under version control.
The missing piece for true reproducibility is the environment that code
runs in. That's what containers give us.
:::

## The problem: "it works on my machine"

- Your analysis runs perfectly... on *your* laptop
- A collaborator runs the same code and it breaks
- Different R version, different package version, different OS
- Reproducible research can't depend on whose computer it is

::: notes
Ask the room: who has hit this? Almost everyone has. Tie it back to any
install friction they felt in Parts 1–3.
:::

## What is a container?

A single file that packages your **entire computing environment**:

- the R installation
- every package, at a pinned version
- the system libraries underneath

> Run that file anywhere → get *exactly* that environment.

::: notes
Emphasis on "entire" and "pinned." This is more than `renv` — it's the
whole stack down to system libraries. Contrast with just sharing a script.
:::

## Why Apptainer (not Docker)?

- Built for **research** and **HPC**
- Runs as *you*, not as root — works on shared clusters
- One portable image file: `analysis.sif`
- The image is the artifact you publish alongside your paper

::: notes
Don't teach Docker by accident. If asked: Docker is great for web services;
Apptainer is the norm in research computing because of the security model on
shared HPC. Same core idea, different conventions.
:::

## The catch — and the lesson {.center}

### Apptainer only runs on **Linux**

There is no Mac or Windows version.

::: notes
Pause here. Let it land as a "problem" before you flip it on the next slide.
:::

## ...which is exactly the point

The host OS **should not** constrain what runs inside.\
But you still need a Linux kernel *somewhere*:

- On a Mac/Windows laptop → a **Codespace** (today)
- On a cluster → the **HPC login node**
- On a Linux laptop → it's just there

::: notes
This single reframe converts the biggest perceived obstacle into the core
mental model. Once you're past the kernel boundary, the container behaves
identically everywhere. Do NOT apologize for the OS switch — name it and use
it.
:::

## Host vs. container

| | Host | Container |
|---|---|---|
| What | Whatever's installed locally | Fixed, pinned image |
| Controlled by | Each user | The definition file |
| Reproducible | By hand, fragile | Yes, by design |
| Use for | Exploration | Sharing / publishing / HPC |

::: notes
Hour 1 was the host (Positron on their laptop). Hour 2 is the container.
Same analysis, both ways — the comparison is the teaching moment.
:::

## Today's workflow

1. **Launch** a Codespace (everyone → identical Linux)
2. **Verify** Apptainer + the pre-built image are present
3. **Run** the DESeq2 pipeline *from* the container
4. **Read** the definition file that built it
5. **Modify** a parameter → re-run → see the result change
6. **Connect** it back to Git

::: notes
We pull a pre-built image rather than building live — building compiles
Bioconductor and takes far too long for a live session. Building from
scratch is the self-paced follow-up.
:::

## Demo: launch + verify {.center}

```bash
apptainer --version
ls -lh ~/deseq2.sif
apptainer exec ~/deseq2.sif R --version
```

::: notes
Live demo cue. Key talking point: there is NO R on this Codespace — R lives
inside the .sif. `apptainer exec` runs a command inside that environment.
Push the Codespace link in chat now so account issues surface early.
:::

## Demo: run the pipeline {.center}

```bash
cd workshops/arcs_04/_materials
apptainer exec ~/deseq2.sif Rscript pipeline.R
ls outputs/
```

::: notes
Same analysis as Hour 1, now on Linux inside a pinned environment, on a
machine that isn't theirs — and the result matches. Open a plot from the
file explorer so the payoff is visual.
:::

## Demo: read the definition {.center}

`_materials/container/deseq2.def`

```default
From: bioconductor/bioconductor_docker:RELEASE_3_19
%post         # install DESeq2, ggplot2 (build time)
%runscript    # default action when you `run` the image
%test         # sanity check at end of build
```

::: notes
The whole environment is one readable text file living next to the code.
Walk each section briefly. Note: changing this file means rebuilding, which
is slow — that's why it's read-only for us today.
:::

## Demo: change and re-run {.center}

In `pipeline.R`:

```r
PADJ <- 0.05   →   PADJ <- 0.01
```

```bash
apptainer exec ~/deseq2.sif Rscript pipeline.R
```

- Significant-gene count changes
- Same image, same data, a controlled change

::: notes
Reproducible ≠ frozen. It means *controlled*. This is the "modify and
observe" moment that earns the Analyze/Create objective without a live
build.
:::

## It all travels together

In the repo, side by side:

- `pipeline.R` — the **code**
- `deseq2.def` — the **environment**
- the published image — `ghcr.io/cwml/deseq2`

> Clone → open Codespace (or HPC) → `apptainer pull` → run → it reproduces.

::: notes
This completes the Part 3 Git story. Code was already versioned; now the
environment is captured too — as a diffable text file and a pullable image.
This is the goal of the whole series, made concrete.
:::

## Recap

- Containers fix "works on my machine"
- Apptainer is Linux-only → use a Codespace / HPC as the kernel
- You **ran** and **modified** a real pipeline from a container
- Code + environment + data now travel together
